title: Conversational ergonomics — a Thread/session API layer (Oracle How-to Guides + API Reference gap)
description: Grounded in a direct, dated (2026-08-02) review of Oracle AI Agent Memory's live How-to Guides (docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/agent-memory/26.4/agmea/ — Store and Search Memory, Use Agent Memory with an MCP Server, Quick Reference Code Samples) plus a follow-up review of the full API Reference (.../agmea/api/index.html — OracleAgentMemory, the Record taxonomy, Scope/SearchScope, OracleThread) against this SDK's current store.py/models.py/types.py. Confirmed already at parity or ahead: get_context_card()'s per-type minimum-result balancing (ORC-1/PIPE-4, store.py:1318 cites Oracle 26.6 by name) and erase_all()/export_scope()/import_scope() (PIPE-5/PIPE-6). Ten genuine, purely ergonomic gaps identified across both reviews — the underlying primitives (remember(), search(), scoped repositories) already do the work, nothing here is new storage capability: (1) Thread object, (2) batch message API, (3) add_memory/add_user/add_agent wrappers, (4) automatic memory extraction, (5) token-budget thread summary, (6) raw-text search() facade, (7) cascading delete_user()/delete_agent(), (8) generic table-agnostic delete_memory(id), (9) async facade for LLM/embedder-calling methods, (10) fuzzy-vs-exact per-dimension scope matching + unscoped-only queries. See the dated 2026-08-02 'EPIC-8 backlog' and 'EPIC-8 addendum' DECISIONS.md entries for the full research writeup, including a substantial list of things deliberately NOT turned into stories (no new Guideline/Fact/Preference tables, no copy of Oracle's default-on fail-fast extraction contract, no copy of its eight token-budget/frequency knobs, no pluggable storage backend, no blanket async-everything, no LLM-backed get_summary) and why each was rejected as scope creep or a philosophy conflict with this SDK's Step 0 'developer-controlled writes' positioning. Designed explicitly for parallel execution: THRD-1/2/3/4/7/8 are fully independent (each appends its own banner-comment method section to MemoryStore, no shared edits) and safe to run as simultaneous subagents/worktrees; THRD-5 depends on THRD-1; THRD-9 depends on THRD-1/3/5; THRD-10 depends on THRD-3; THRD-6 (the Thread facade) depends on THRD-1..5 and must run last. THRD-10 is explicitly flagged as the highest-blast-radius story — it must not touch _scope_predicates()/MemoryScope, the VER-5-audited scope-isolation core. Same Step 0 philosophy as every prior epic: Db2-only, zero mandatory new infrastructure, every new hook opt-in and leaving default behavior unchanged.
